original_source_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the underlying category $\mathcal{C}$ is a
full subcategory of $\Sch/S$,
\item any Zariski covering of $T \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
can be refined by a covering of $\mathcal{C}$,
\item $S/S$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}$,
\item every covering of $\mathcal{C}$ is an fpqc covering of schemes.
\end{enumerate}
Then the presheaf $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$ and
any quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-module on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
is of the form $\mathcal{F}^a$ for some quasi-coherent sheaf
$\mathcal{F}$ on $S$.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal C$ a site whose underlying category is a full subcategory of $\mathrm{Sch}/S$, containing $S$, whose coverings are fpqc as scheme families, and such that every Zariski cover of any object admits a refinement by a $\mathcal C$-cover. Let $\mathcal O(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ be the structure-ring presheaf. For a quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $S$, define $\mathcal F^a(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,(T\to S)^*\mathcal F)$. A *quasi-coherent module over the ringed site* $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is an $\mathcal O$-module which locally on a covering is a cokernel of a morphism between (possibly infinite) direct sums of copies of $\mathcal O$.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the underlying category $\mathcal{C}$ is a
full subcategory of $\Sch/S$,
\item any Zariski covering of $T \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$
can be refined by a covering of $\mathcal{C}$,
\item $S/S$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}$,
\item every covering of $\mathcal{C}$ is an fpqc covering of schemes.
\end{enumerate}
Then the presheaf $\mathcal{O}$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$ and
any quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-module on $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
is of the form $\mathcal{F}^a$ for some quasi-coherent sheaf
$\mathcal{F}$ on $S$.

**Scope and interpretation:** No big/small site identification is assumed silently: the four exact stated site conditions are necessary. The conclusion is *essential surjectivity* of F↦F^a; the structure presheaf O is a sheaf by fpqc descent.
